title: Shareable Map Link Helper: Links and Embeds
description: Build shareable map links and simple embeds for a place with the Shareable Map Link Helper — no API key, copy and paste. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a small business's 'visit us' page can carry a live embedded map of its exact corner — built from one address, with no developer and no API key.
quick_answer: The Shareable Map Link Helper builds the link and embed forms of a map view — the shareable URL, the directions link and the simple iframe embed — from one place or coordinate pair. Enter the location, choose the form, and copy code that works anywhere.

Invites with a real map embed get fewer lost guests than invites with a typed address — the venue pin carries parking-lot precision.
A neighbourhood embed sells the area honestly — the pin is the property; the map around it is the context buyers actually judge.
Meetup points, trailheads and pitch locations embedded once serve every season's newcomers without a webmaster.
A link takes the reader away to the map; an embed brings the map to your page. Same underlying view, opposite journeys — choose by whether your page or the map should keep the reader.

A directions link opens with the destination pre-filled and asks only 'from where?' — one field between your visitor and a route. It is the highest-converting form of map sharing a small site can use.

faq: Do I need an API key for the embed?
Not for the standard iframe embed forms this helper builds — they load the provider's public embed. Key-based APIs are a developer product with quotas; a copy-paste embed is not that.
Will the embed slow my page?
It loads when the page does; lazy-loading the iframe (a one-word attribute) defers it until scrolled to. The helper's output accepts the attribute cleanly.
Can the pin be an address instead of coordinates?
Yes — place names and addresses resolve to the map's own point. For survey-exact pins, coordinates are the unambiguous input.
Embeds are responsive in modern site builders; the link forms hand off to the native map app, which mobile readers usually prefer anyway.
Can I style or brand the embed?
The public embed wears the provider's design. Branded, styled maps are the key-based APIs' territory — an honest boundary of the free form.
Directions links ask the reader's map app for the start — their own location, with their permission, in their app. Your page never sees it.
One view, one focus pin is the embed's grammar. Multi-pin maps are the Store Locator Map Builder's job.
Is sharing a map of my home wise?
Share the neighbourhood zoom, not the doorstep pin — the zoom choice is a privacy dial, and this helper makes it yours to set.
